report: Markedly elevated ALP/GGT with mild transaminases indicates cholestasis. Ultrasound/MRI localize to hepatic hilum. Biopsy showing PAX8-positive malignant cells with bile duct destruction is gold-standard for metastatic carcinoma, explaining secondary cholestatic injury. Enzymes remained elevated despite stopping alcohol/axitinib; viral/autoimmune/metabolic liver disease absent, excluding drug-induced and chronic liver disease. Thus metastatic carcinoma at hepatic hilum is the cause.
answer: Diffuse type of liver metastasis from renal cell carcinoma
